messages.subject: GGIR sleep duration issue
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I have been using the GeneActiv to capture sleep data for my research. I have been able to successfully extract the data but the last couple of times it seems that the analysis isn't integrating the manual sleep log properly as it shows the time earlier than stated and the wake time later than stated.

The code that I am using is the following:

library(GGIR)
g.shell.GGIR(#=======================================
             # INPUT NEEDED:
             mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
             datadir="//campus.gla.ac.uk/SSD_Home_Data_D/2488274M/My <http://campus.gla.ac.uk/SSD_Home_Data_D/2488274M/My> Documents/Baseline Assessments",
             outputdir="//campus.gla.ac.uk/SSD_Home_Data_D/2488274M/My <http://campus.gla.ac.uk/SSD_Home_Data_D/2488274M/My> Documents/Output_019",
             f0=1, f1=2,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 1:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: reading file, auto-calibration, and extracting features
             do.enmo = TRUE,             do.anglez=TRUE,
             desiredtz="Europe/London",
             chunksize=1,                printsummary=TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 2:
             #-------------------------------
             strategy = 2,               ndayswindow=7,
             hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
             maxdur = 9,                 includedaycrit = 16,
             winhr = c(5,10),
             qlevels = c(c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440)),
             qwindow=c(0,24),
             ilevels = c(seq(0,400,by=50),8000),
             mvpathreshold =c(100,120),
             bout.metric = 4,
             closedbout=FALSE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 3:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Sleep detection
             timethreshold= c(5),        anglethreshold=5,
             ignorenonwear = TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 4:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Integrating sleep log (if available) with sleep detection
             # storing day and person specific summaries of sleep
             excludefirstlast = FALSE,
             includenightcrit = 16,
             def.noc.sleep = c(),
             loglocation= "//campus.gla.ac.uk/SSD_Home_Data_D/2488274M/My <http://campus.gla.ac.uk/SSD_Home_Data_D/2488274M/My> Documents/Ayan/Sleep Logs/Sleep Study_Sleep Log 019.csv",
             outliers.only = TRUE,
             criterror = 4,
             relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
             sleeplogidnum = FALSE,
             colid=1,
             coln1=2,
             do.visual = TRUE,
             nnights = 7,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 5:
             # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
             #-------------------------------
             threshold.lig = c(30), threshold.mod = c(100),  threshold.vig = c(400),
             boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(1),   timewindow = c("WW"),
             #-----------------------------------
             # Report generation
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Generating reports based on meta-data
             do.report=c(2,4,5),
             visualreport=TRUE,     dofirstpage = TRUE,
             viewingwindow=1)

When I extract the data the average sleep time starts at 9 pm and wake up time as 8 am when the sleep log shows 12am as bedtime and wake up time at 6.30.

I am sure why this issue has come up and I was wondering if anyone had any suggestions?

Cheers!
Ayan

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] what is (dur_day_total_MOD_min)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Maher, see my answers below:

‐‐‐‐‐‐‐ Original Message ‐‐‐‐‐‐‐

On Tuesday, June 8th, 2021 at 03:08, Maher AL-Quaimi <malq...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Dears, I have two "basic" questions. When I read the discerption for
>
> dur_day_total_MOD_min
> (Total duration of day in minutes of moderate activity during the day) is that the mean during all days of it is the sum of moderate activity ?

The daysummary report only shows totals and averages per recording day.
The person summary report shows the averages of day-level variables across recordings days. None of these variables tries to tell you the total time spent per week or per recording. However, you can derive this by multiplying the person level variables related to time-use to get the weekly totals. Multiple by 7 if it refers to average of all days, by 5 for variables specific to weekdays, or by 2 for variables specific to weekend days.

> 2nd question, what does GGIR stand for ? I remember seeing it before but I can't find it now. sorry if my questions seems very basic !

See: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#59_What_does_GGIR_stand_for

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Short periods of detected wear-time
messages.body_plain:
Hi Natascja,

At the moment there is no option to change this setting of the code.
Did you use a non-wear and nap diary? If yes, could it be an option that for your specific study design you ignore GGIR's non-wear detection (set argument do.imp=FALSE) and you rely on your diary data to decide whether a day should be included?

On the other hand, if we would try to make this modifiable then it would be good to have some way of validating the solution and to develop guidance for GGIR users about how to use this optional modification to the non-wear detection.

As you may be aware I usually respond to significant GGIR enhancement requests with: You are welcome to implement it yourself or find someone in your environment who can, or I can do it as a paid consultancy given that GGIR is open source my time investment cannot be for free.

Thanks,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant
https://accelting.com/

 <https://accelting.com/>

‐‐‐‐‐‐‐ Original Message ‐‐‐‐‐‐‐

On Monday, May 31st, 2021 at 21:36, Natascja Di Cristofaro <natascja....@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hello,
> We have toddlers wearing accelerometers during their waking hours to measure their habitual physical activity. We're encountering an issue of days being misclassified as non-wear due to toddlers' shorter wear periods and long naps. Is there any way to modify the algorithm that determines the plausibility of “wear-periods” in-between non-wear periods?
>
> The following is stated in the vignette:
> All detected wear-periods of less than six hours and less than 30% of the combined duration of their bordering non-wear periods were classified as non-wear. Additionally, all wear-periods of less than three hours and which formed less than 80% of their bordering non-wear periods were classified as non-wear.
>
> Is there any code that can remove/modify the % of non-wear it needs to meet?
>
> Thanks,
> Natascja
>
>

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GGIR sleep duration issue
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ayan,

Can you check the following:

- Use GGIR's g.loadlog() function as documented in https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/GGIR.pdf. This would allow you to check that the sleeplog is correctly loaded.
- Check that sleeplog is used by GGIR, by looking at the 'guider' columns, this should state that sleeplog was used. If not, then maybe something went wrong with specifying the filepath.
- Checkout the part4 reports in the QC folder, which have a column for both the guider (sleeplog in your case) and the estimates based on fuse information from sleeplog and accelerometer.

Best, Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant

messages.subject: GGIR 2.4-0 on CRAN
messages.body_plain:
Dear GGIR list,

Just in case you missed it: Last week GGIR 2.4-0 was released.

The main addition is the incorporation of 28 metrics of daytime behavioural fragmentation. See vignette sections https://bit.ly/3wUy8Bg & https://bit.ly/3vVrMBD.
I am aware that documentation narrative could be improved, but this is at least an accurate minimalistic description.

Big thanks to Mathilde Chen, Manasa Yerramalla, and Séverine Sabia from https://cress-umr1153.fr/index.php/epiageing/ for all your support, brainstorming, and testing for this new functionality!

Best wishes,
Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant

messages.body_plain:
Thank you so much for explaining it. It helps a lot.

On Friday, April 9, 2021 at 4:42:58 AM UTC-4 Vincent van Hees wrote:
> That function is used by GGIR internally, as a user you should not have to worry about it.
> So, if all goes well GGIR automatically takes in account DST.
>
> In GGIR part 2 output you should see this in the fact that DST nights will results in 25 or 23 measurement hours in a day. Further, in the part 4 output you will notice that when sleep starts before DST and ends after DST it will one hour more or one hour less in sleep duration compared to what you would expect from the start and end clock time.

Julia

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Frequency of raw acc data
messages.body_plain:
Dear Claire,

I think the answer to your question may depend on sensor brand and data is sampled or resampled. Also, the answer may be specific to your behavioural outcome of interest.

Intuitively I would expect no influence on GGIR's sleep detection, because the sleep detection only relies on rolling median. Magnitude of movement might be affected depending on how resampling is done. I think more research is needed to make strong statements about this.

Note that Scott Small has been doing work in this direction, see pre-print here: https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.10.22.20217927v1

Best, Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GGIR for waist worn assessment
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dylan,

Thanks for your message and sorry for the slow reply. I am currently working on a two projects that relate to your question.

You are correct that many of the default GGIR argument values are tailored to wrist-worn accelerometer. However, GGIR is designed to be adaptable to any sensor location. There are about half a dozen of publications that have proposed cut-points for hip or waist worn accelerometers to study physical activity, you can use those cut-points in GGIR. So, I think a basic physical activity analysis is already possible.

Less well understood is the value of GGIR's sleep detection for waist-worn accelerometers. If you know of any polysomnography data sets where an accelerometer was worn on the wrist then that would be great. Also, datasets with sleep diary and hip-worn accelerometer could be valuable.

Let me know if you want to chat, and we we can explore how you best contribute.

Best wishes,
Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant
